claims.statement: The llama-helper sidecar speaks a line-delimited JSON protocol over stdin/stdout with serde-tagged messages: requests are generate (prompt, max_tokens, context_size, model_path, temperature, top_k, top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, repeat_penalty, penalty_last_n, stop_tokens), ping, and shutdown; responses are response {text, error}, pong, goodbye, and error {message}. Diagnostics go to stderr, which the parent inherits. The Rust client mirrors only the Generate variant of Request in client.rs, while SidecarManager emits ping/shutdown as ad-hoc json! objects.

In llama-helper, model-load failures and generation failures are reported as a response message with the error field set (the loop continues), while only an unparseable request line produces the error variant. max_tokens defaults to 512 and context_size to 2048 when omitted, and stop tokens are stripped from the accumulated output before returning. Sampling defaults in SamplingConfig::from_request are defensive: non-finite/negative temperature becomes 0.0 (greedy), top_k defaults to 64 with floor 1, top_p defaults to 0.95 forced to 1.0 unless in (0,1], penalties floored at 0/non-negative, repeat_penalty 1.0 and forced positive, penalty_last_n default 0; a penalty sampler stage is prepended only when penalty_last_n > 0 and at least one penalty deviates from neutral.

Both sides of the sidecar pipe honor the LLAMA_IDLE_TIMEOUT environment variable (seconds, default 300). The helper checks idle time before each stdin read and emits goodbye then exits on expiry or on a shutdown request; stdin EOF also terminates it. The app passes its configured timeout to the spawned process.

llama-helper computes GPU layer offload from detected VRAM (Metal via sysctl hw.memsize assuming ~60% of system memory, CUDA via nvidia-smi free memory, else conservative 4 GB), estimating model layers from file size (>2.5 GB means 33, else 28) and budgeting per-layer weights plus KV cache (0.25 GB per 1k context for large models, 0.12 GB otherwise) against VRAM minus a 0.5 GB safety margin; unreadable model file size forces CPU-only. Inference threads are max(1, cores/2 + 2) to avoid starving the UI; context and batch size both use context_size; the prompt is tokenized with AddBos::Always; sampling is greedy for temperature <= 0 else penalties/top_k/top_p/temp/dist seeded from wall-clock ms; token pieces are incrementally UTF-8 decoded with a buffer-retry on InsufficientBufferSpace, stopping on max_tokens, an end-of-generation token, or a stop-token match.

SidecarManager::resolve_helper_binary resolves the helper binary in a fixed order: the MEETILY_LLAMA_HELPER env var if it exists, then next to the current executable (exact llama-helper-<target triple>[.exe] then a fuzzy match on any file starting with llama-helper not ending in .d), then RESOURCE_DIR with the same matching, then dev workspace target/release|debug paths from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR; failing all, it errors with build instructions. The target triple comes from the TARGET env var or per-platform cfg. The fuzzy fallback exists because Tauri externalBin bundling renames the binary to llama-helper-<triple> beside the executable, which tauri.conf.json declares under bundle.externalBin as binaries/llama-helper.

SidecarManager::spawn shuts down any existing process first, then spawns the helper with piped stdin/stdout, inherited stderr, and LLAMA_IDLE_TIMEOUT set from its configured timeout. On Unix it launches through nice -n 10; on Windows it sets CREATE_NO_WINDOW | BELOW_NORMAL_PRIORITY_CLASS. After storing handles it marks is_healthy, resets should_shutdown, records current_model_path, and starts the health-check and idle-check loops.

Two spawned background loops supervise the sidecar and both exit when should_shutdown is set. The health check runs every 30 s, skips when unhealthy or when active requests exist, and on a failed ping (5 s timeout) clears is_healthy; it deliberately bypasses send_request so health pings never inflate active_request_count. The idle check runs every 60 s; while requests are active it refreshes last_activity instead of timing out, otherwise it shuts the sidecar down once idle time exceeds the timeout.

send_request wraps each call in a RequestGuard that RAII-increments/decrements active_request_count, writes the JSON line plus newline and flushes, then awaits one stdout line under tokio::time::timeout; an empty line read means the sidecar's stdout closed (crash/exit) and errors. On timeout the manager shuts the sidecar down entirely - the protocol has no cancel message, so process termination is the only way to stop a running generation. ensure_running short-circuits only when current_model_path matches and the process is healthy; anything else triggers a full shutdown and respawn.

Sidecar shutdown has three paths: shutdown_gracefully sets should_shutdown and polls active_request_count every 500 ms for up to 10 minutes before calling shutdown; shutdown sends the shutdown line if healthy (errors ignored), waits up to 3 s for exit, then kills and clears all handles/model path/health; the Drop impl only sets should_shutdown since async cleanup cannot run in Drop.

At the client layer, shutdown_sidecar_gracefully detaches the manager from the SIDECAR_MANAGER global and drains active requests in a spawned background task; it is called when the user saves a model configuration (api/api.rs) so a provider/model switch retires the old sidecar without blocking the UI. force_shutdown_sidecar detaches and calls shutdown() directly and is invoked from RunEvent::Exit in lib.rs so the helper never outlives the app.

client.rs holds the sidecar behind a lazy_static global SIDECAR_MANAGER (Arc<Mutex<Option<Arc<SidecarManager>>>>); generate_with_builtin lazily creates and installs a manager on first use, and init_sidecar_manager/is_sidecar_healthy operate on the same global. A MODEL_PATH_CACHE Lazy<RwLock<HashMap>> read-through cache over models::get_model_path re-validates that the file still exists on hits (a deleted model invalidates the entry), double-checks after acquiring the write lock, and errors if the resolved GGUF is absent.

generate_with_builtin is the single BuiltInAI generation entry point: it looks up the ModelDef, resolves the cached model path, formats the prompt via the model's chat template, sanitizes the model's sampling preset, and sends a generate request with DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 4096 and the model's context_size under GENERATION_TIMEOUT_SECS = 900. An optional CancellationToken is checked before start, after sidecar startup, and before parsing, and is raced against the request via tokio::select! - mid-generation cancellation shuts the sidecar down to stop token generation.

summary/llm_client.rs routes the BuiltInAI provider (parsed from "builtin-ai", "local-llama", or "localllama") to generate_with_builtin before the HTTP provider path, requiring an app_data_dir for model resolution; all other providers go through HTTP chat-completion APIs.

summary_engine's ModelManager deliberately mirrors the whisper/parakeet engine patterns: it reuses the same ModelStatus shape (with NotDownloaded where those engines use Missing, including the Corrupted {file_size, expected_min_size} variant) and the same MB-based DownloadProgress struct (downloaded_mb, total_mb, speed_mbps, percent). Models live in app_data_dir/models/summary and status is a serde-tagged enum surfaced to the frontend.

get_available_models() in models.rs is the extension point for adding local models; the catalog is qwen3.5:2b (Qwen3.5-2B-Q4_K_M.gguf, 1221 MB, 24 layers), qwen3.5:4b (2614 MB, 32 layers), gemma3:4b (gemma-3-4b-it-Q4_K_M.gguf, 2374 MB, 35 layers), and gemma3:1b (gemma-3-1b-it-Q8_0.gguf, 1019 MB, 26 layers), all with context_size 32768, downloaded from Hugging Face (unsloth for Qwen, bartowski for Gemma), with qwen35_summary sampling and stop token <|im_end|> for Qwen and gemma3_instruct with <end_of_turn> for Gemma. Each ModelDef also names its prompt template and its name is persisted in the database as the model field when provider="builtin-ai".

SamplingParams::sanitize_for_llama_helper normalizes presets before they cross the wire (NaN/negative temperature becomes 0.0, out-of-range top_p becomes 1.0, negative penalties become 0, non-positive repeat_penalty becomes 1.0, negative penalty_last_n becomes 0, top_k floored at 0). Prompt templates are static strings: the qwen3.5_nonthinking template opens the assistant turn with an empty think block for direct-response summaries, and format_prompt escapes user-supplied control markers (<|im_start|>, <|im_end|>, <start_of_turn>, <end_of_turn>, <think>, </think>) in the user prompt so transcript content cannot break the template.

download_model_detailed enforces one active download per model and handles existing files by size: within a 10 percent window of expected it short-circuits to Available; larger than expected it deletes and re-downloads; smaller it resumes via an HTTP Range request, appending on 206 Partial Content or restarting fresh otherwise. The reqwest client uses tcp_nodelay, a 1 h overall timeout, and a 30 s connect timeout, writing through an 8 MB BufWriter; progress reports on percent change or every 500 ms with speed from bytes since the last report.

During download, a 30-second per-chunk timeout detects stalled connections and stream errors are categorized (timeout/connect/body) into user-facing messages; both set ModelStatus::Error so the UI can offer retry. User cancellation is a per-model flag checked per chunk: the partial file is flushed and kept for resume, the model returns to NotDownloaded, and the error carries a CANCELLED: prefix so the command layer can distinguish it from real failures. After completion the file is validated by GGUF magic number (GGUF plus legacy ggjt/ggla/ggml); an invalid file is deleted and the model lands in Error.

scan_models (run at init and refreshable) classifies each catalog entry's file by size against the expected window: within the window it is Available, outside it is Corrupted {file_size, expected_min_size}, unreadable metadata becomes Error, and missing files are NotDownloaded; an actively-downloading model keeps its in-memory Downloading status instead of being rescanned. is_model_ready(name, refresh) optionally rescans before answering. delete_model removes the GGUF file and resets status to NotDownloaded.

builtin_ai_download_model streams progress through the builtin-ai-download-progress Tauri event (model, progress, downloaded_mb, total_mb, speed_mbps). The progress callback always emits status "downloading"; the completed event with status "completed" is emitted by the command only after the download task fully finishes including validation; real errors emit status "error" with the message; cancellations emit nothing from this path because the cancel command already emitted a "cancelled" event. The frontend listens in BuiltInModelManager.tsx, OnboardingContext, and the onboarding/toast components.

builtin_ai_get_available_summary_model forces a fresh scan and returns the Available model with the highest priority, ordered qwen3.5:4b > qwen3.5:2b > gemma3:4b > gemma3:1b. builtin_ai_get_recommended_model returns qwen3.5:4b when system RAM is at least 14 GB, else qwen3.5:2b, regardless of platform - pinned by tests at the 13/14 GB boundary. The command's doc comment still describes an older 8 GB / macOS-specific rule that the implementation no longer follows.

lib.rs manages ModelManagerState (an Arc<Mutex<Option<Arc<ModelManager>>>>) and registers the eight builtin_ai_* commands: list_models, get_model_info, download_model, cancel_download, delete_model, is_model_ready, get_available_summary_model, and get_recommended_model. init_model_manager_at_startup runs in a spawned task during setup using app_data_dir/models/summary; if it fails, each command lazily initializes the manager on demand.

The TypeScript wrapper BuiltInAIAPI.getModelsDirectory() invokes builtin_ai_get_models_directory, but no such Tauri command exists in the Rust backend (commands.rs defines only the eight builtin_ai_* commands) and it is not registered in lib.rs, so that wrapper call cannot succeed.

llama-helper is a workspace member pinning llama-cpp-2 = "=0.1.146" with metal/cuda/vulkan features that forward to the llama-cpp-2 backend (no coreml; the GPU build script maps a detected coreml to metal). Its release profile optimizes for size (codegen-units = 1, lto = true, opt-level = "s") to keep startup fast and the bundle small.

Every build path builds the helper separately before tauri build and copies the binary to frontend/src-tauri/binaries/llama-helper-<target triple>[.exe]. build-gpu.sh builds with the detected GPU feature, detects the triple via rustc -vV, removes stale llama-helper* binaries, and copies from target/release. CI (build.yml) builds macOS with --features metal and Windows/Linux release builds CPU-only (the Windows release path cites a CMake race in llama-cpp-sys-2 Vulkan builds while the app itself still uses Vulkan for Whisper); build-macos.yml uses metal, build-linux.yml and build-windows.yml are CPU-only, and build-devtest.yml builds vulkan on Windows.

tauri.conf.json declares the sidecar under bundle.externalBin as binaries/llama-helper alongside binaries/ffmpeg; Tauri appends the target triple when bundling, which is exactly the filename resolve_helper_binary searches for next to the installed executable.

Focused tests cover the protocol and policy surfaces: llama-helper tests assert that omitted penalty fields default to neutral (disabling the penalty chain) and that a full Qwen-style penalty set deserializes and activates uses_penalties; client.rs tests assert request serialization emits "type":"generate" with all sampling fields and that response/error messages deserialize; models.rs tests pin catalog metadata for all four models, template formatting including the Qwen empty think block, control-marker escaping, and sanitize_for_llama_helper clamping; commands.rs tests pin the 14 GB recommendation boundary and summary_model_priority ordering.
